summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — ADSK +8%, EXPE +7%, CHTR +7%, DASH +7%, CPRT +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (SNDK -14%, GLW -12%, LITE -9%, COHR -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: SNDK (-13.56%) — Third straight double-digit drop as NAND pricing/demand fears, Chinese memory competition, and AI-capex sustainability doubts unwind SNDK's parabolic run from >$2,350 in June. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNDK is a former Western Digital spinoff whose price (>$1,000/sh) and realized volatility (50%+ drawdown in a month, three consecutive double-digit-% sessions) sit far outside typical universe price/volatility screens.

top_movers.catalyst: Guggenheim initiated ADSK at Buy on billings/revenue upside and AI-resilience; also buoyed by its $3.6B MaintainX acquisition announcement.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ADSK is a large-cap AEC/software name not currently tracked, so no filter was ever exposed to today's gap; the move was analyst-upgrade + M&A driven rather than a pattern a technical scanner would catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sell-side rating-change/initiation feed that auto-admits large-cap names into the tradable universe intraday when a >2-notch upgrade or >5% pre-market gap is detected.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued rally off Expedia's exclusive 12-month Allegiant Airlines distribution deal (566 routes, 124 cities) plus reaffirmed FY26 revenue guidance of $15.6-16.0B.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — EXPE sits in travel/OTA, a sector the bot's current universes (tech/momentum-focused large caps) don't cover despite EXPE's large-cap liquidity.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap travel/OTA names (EXPE, BKNG, ABNB) to the universe screen since they pass standard liquidity/market-cap filters; alternatively add a cross-sector partnership/M&A news scanner that flags >5% movers outside the current universe for manual review.

top_movers.catalyst: Multi-day recovery rally after Q2 EPS beat ($10.66 vs $10.37 est) despite revenue miss/broadband losses, fueled by Cox merger nearing Aug close and ongoing SpaceX/Starlink mobile-partnership speculation.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CHTR is legacy cable/telecom (Communication Services), a sector/category likely excluded from momentum and mean-reversion universes, and the move sits inside a post-earnings (7/24) event window bots typically blackout for gap risk.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings gap-continuation gate: names reporting within the last 5 sessions become eligible if price holds ≥5% above pre-earnings close and above VWAP, instead of a blanket earnings-window exclusion.

top_movers.catalyst: DoorDash received FAA Part 135 air-carrier certification and launched 'DoorDash Air,' its in-house commercial drone delivery program.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DASH is a ~$91B consumer-internet/gig-delivery name; the bot's tracked lists likely exclude this sector bucket or haven't been refreshed to add a name that grew into large-cap status.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a periodic universe-refresh job that re-screens NASDAQ/NYSE names by market cap and includes consumer-internet/gig-economy tickers >$50B cap, rather than relying on a static sector-restricted list.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh news today; relief rally as Jay Adair's July 31 return as CEO (announced June 29) nears, with stock recovering off a post-announcement/YTD selloff low.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (large-cap auto-salvage/services name not covered by tradable sector list). Even if covered, this is a slow-burn sentiment recovery tied to a leadership-transition date, not a single-session earnings/news gap a catalyst-scanner would flag intraday.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a leadership-transition/8-K event tag that flags names within 5 trading days of an announced CEO change effective date for temporary universe inclusion, since sentiment repricing often clusters around the effective date rather than the announcement date.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-day news event; continuation of a multi-day pre-earnings run-up in travel/OTA stocks as Mideast ceasefire eased oil prices and a flagged 3pt demand headwind ahead of Aug 4 Q2 print.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — BKNG is a consumer-discretionary/travel mega-cap, a sector the bot's universe construction apparently doesn't cover, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate the multi-day momentum.
top_movers.suggestion: Rebuild universe inclusion from a market-cap/liquidity screen (e.g. top-N by ADV regardless of sector) rather than a static sector-limited list, so travel/consumer-discretionary mega-caps like BKNG aren't structurally excluded.

top_movers.catalyst: Third straight double-digit drop as NAND pricing/demand fears, Chinese memory competition, and AI-capex sustainability doubts unwind SNDK's parabolic run from >$2,350 in June.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNDK is a former Western Digital spinoff whose price (>$1,000/sh) and realized volatility (50%+ drawdown in a month, three consecutive double-digit-% sessions) sit far outside typical universe price/volatility screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a volatility-aware universe override: admit normally-excluded high-price/high-ATR names once realized 20-day vol exceeds a threshold (e.g. >80% annualized), so mean-reversion strategies can catch post-selloff bounces in ex-universe mega-movers.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 beat (core EPS $0.78, sales +17%) but Q3 guidance underwhelmed vs AI-optical hype; stock sold off ~12% on 'sell the news' reaction.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GLW is a large-cap industrials/specialty-glass name, likely excluded by sector filters tuned to tech/semis, or by a blanket earnings-day blackout that skips all reporters regardless of gap direction.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings gap-release rule: names with a pre-market gap ≥8% on reported earnings get admitted to the momentum universe for that session instead of being blanket-excluded by the earnings blackout.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news; sector-wide AI-photonics selloff (Coherent, AOI, LITE all down 9-12%) on profit-taking/OpenAI IPO-delay jitters after a 71% YTD run.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LITE is a large-cap optical/photonics component name (AI-infra supplier), a sector/category the bot's universes don't cover, and its extreme historical volatility (52-wk range $101-$1085) likely falls outside typical universe volatility/beta caps anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an AI-infrastructure/photonics sector bucket (LITE, COHR, AAOI) to at least one sector-rotation or mean-reversion universe with a volatility-adjusted position cap, so post-selloff bounces in this crowded trade are catchable.

top_movers.catalyst: No firm-specific news; broad profit-taking/rotation across crowded AI-optics names (COHR, AOI, LITE) after a big 2026 rally, amplified by an insider share sale.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — COHR is a $61B photonics/optical-components supplier tied to AI-datacenter capex, a sector bucket the bot's universes don't currently cover.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an 'AI-infrastructure/photonics' sector tag (COHR, LITE, AOI, etc.) to at least one momentum or sector-rotation strategy's universe so crowded-trade unwinds like this become visible.
